steps.text: Place pork roast in a slow cooker.
Stir together cranberry sauce, onion, and salad dressing in a medium bowl; pour over pork roast.
Cook on Low for 8 hours or High for 4 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of roast should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Cranberry Pork
raw_recipe.description: Cranberry sauce, French salad dressing, and sliced onions go for a long, slow simmer with a juicy pork roast.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Cranberry Pork

review.reviewBody: Like many other reviewers the sparse number of ingrediants combined with the thought of cranberry sauce & French dressing made us skeptical but in the end it was good & we plan to make it again. I did use fresh crushed garlic & rubbed it on all sides of our 3.5lb pork tenderloin followed by a light application of salt & pepper before placing it in our crock pot. My advice on the "sauce" is to mix the dressing & cranberries BEFORE adding the onion to the mix as the onions make it difficult to thoroughly mix otherwise. Our tenderloin took only 6 hrs on low but was moist and tasty & perfect for a day when you need something easy that you can start & let cook without any tending to. My wife did use "Wondra" to thicken the sauce.

Improvised with 1.5 lb pork tenderloin. I used small can of cranberry sauce, 1/ 3 C of Catalina w/bacon dressing (what I had on hand) and cooked for 2.5 hours on high. Everything else as recipe stated. Turned out very, very good. I will definitely make it again.

I trimmed my 4.5 pound pork tenderloin and cut it in half to make sure it would get done in time. I seasoned with garlic powder and lemon pepper, substituted dry onion soup mix for the fresh onion, mixing it in with whole berry cranberry sauce and Catalina French (used what I had.) I added a little corn starch, will add a little more next time to thicken the sauce. Four hours on high in the slow cooker was perfect. I took out the cooked meat and let it rest 10 min before slicing. Meanwhile I mixed a little more cornstarch with a half cup of the liquid, then mixed it back into the crock and cooked half an hour to thicken the sauce. I couldn't believe how easy, moist, tender, and yummy this was, I will gladly fix it again, exactly the same way, maybe for company next time. Would be good with rice or mashed potatoes. Excellent recipe!

WOW!!! I used WHOLE cranberry sauce & 1/2 cup Catalina dressing. Put 1 lb of baby carrots under meat & thick sliced yellow onion over meat. Topped with the sauce. Cooked 2 hrs on HIGH & then 4 hrs on LOW. Then house smells wonderful, was 5 minutes work & FANTASTIC! Family & I are now addicted. Will be making once a week!

In agreement with other reviewers, I was skeptical about the sauce but it turned out delicious! I used Lite Honey French dressing (the only kind in the house). I also made homemade whole cranberry sauce.
I followed the recipe exactly. I did not season the pork at all and it tasted great. 
I took the advice of other reviewers and mixed the cranberry sauce and dressing first before adding the onion. 
I put everything in the cooker at noon on high. At 4pm, the meat temperature was 180 degrees F. I reduced it to low until 7pm. The meat was nice and tender. Once I dished out the meat, I added corn starch and water to the sauce to thicken it.
I paired the pork with mashed potatoes and broccoli.
This recipe is great during the fall and winter but I may make it year round since it was so delicious! Was a hit with the entire family.

As other reviews have stated, the ingredients in this recipe can make you skeptical that it will be good. This dish was delicious. I followed other reviewers recommendations and used whole cranberry sauce as well as coating the pork in salt, pepper and garlic. I let the pork sit with the ingredients overnight. I also used another reviewers suggestion of creating a rue with the sauce. I used 1T OF both butter and flour, after heating mixed in the sauce. 

I also cooked the pork on low in the slow cooker and within 6 hours it was complete. Less than I had anticipated.

This was so delicious. For once I can't think of anything that I would need to add to make this recipe more incredible. Will definitely be making this again in the future.

My mom showed me how to make this and it is super easy and delicious! Instead of onions she told me to use 1 packet of Lipton Onion Soup. I love that you can prepare this in your slow cooker the night before and then cook it on low all day while you are at work.
I've made this several times. I take about 1/2 a cup of the liquid out shortly before its done and mix in 2 tablespoons of corn starch. It makes a really good thick sauce for with the pork.

I made this but due to being in a rush I changed the recipe a bit. I used Catalina dressing instead of French (it's what the store had and I saw another reviewer did the same), I added an extra can of the cranberry sauce but with whole berries and I didn't want to chop an onion (dirty dishes) so I used a packet of onion soup mix. IT TURNED OUT AMAZING. The pork was a little dry, but with the sauce on it, it was fine. A bit of the tanginess was lost when reheated, but my boyfriend preferred the sweeter sauce. It's his new favorite pork dish, I will be making again.

This dish was easy to follow but I made a few changes.

I rubbed the pork tenderloin with olive oil, minced garlic, salt & pepper. In a hot pan seared the meat on all sides and added the sliced onions and lightly browned. Add onions to the bottom of the crock pot, then pork and covered with cranberry jelly and French dressing mixture. I added a few handfuls of dried cranberries. Cooked on low for 3 hours. I added a few tsps. of cornstarch to thicken up the sauce. Served with mashed potatoes and grilled vegetables. My husband and 3 sons enjoyed it.

I wasn't sure I really liked this but everyone else loved it. My pork roast was smaller than what was called for so I ended up with a lot of extra liquid after it was done. I saved the liquid and simmered pork chops in it for another dinner. I think if I try this recipe again, I will try substituting the vinegar with wine. The only vinegar in this recipe is in the French dressing and as I make my own, it may have been a little more vinegar than works in this dish. That being said, I used the leftover sauce slow cooking pork chops... Superb!

We really enjoyed this recipe. Usually do a more savory option for the pork loin, but this was a nice finish with a slightly sweet finish. the drippings make for a really nice gravy. With the extra gravy I'm going to attempt to make a elevated poutine with brie cheese curds. The cranberry and pork gravy will make a nice festive twist to a Canadian classic :)

This is such a simple recipe to make and it tastes so good. I've made it for a couple of years now, but today I decided to add potatoes to the mix. The potatoes were delicious and the sauce was a little thicker so that made that a plus. I am definitely going to do it with with cut potatoes all the time
I made this once before using another dressing like Catalina, very good.I watched the time to be sure it was not overcooked.

I made this tonight. It was absolutely delicious. I will be making it again. I made the recipe as given but used two 1 1/2lb pork tenderloins. My fiancé loved it too. I served it with roasted potatoes and peas...perfect!
So very easy to make. It tasted good enough for my company to have seconds!

Wow…..I did what you should never do ….have company over and try a new recipe lol. This was so good and tender. I followed the recipe as well as reviews to preseason the pork with salt, pepper and garlic. Company loved it and I will be making this again for sure. It’s a keeper.

I wish I could rate this six stars! Thank you, Dawn Miner, for a simple, quick, and delicious recipe. I used two small pork loin roasts, and rubbed pork spice into the meat. That’s the only change - otherwise followed the recipe and cooked it on high for 3.5 hours. The house smelled wonderful while it cooked. Delicious with rice, lots of sauce. I will be making this again and again.
It was ok. Don’t know that I’d make it again.
